title: Knowingly owning or operating a chop shop
summary: Knowingly and intentionally owning or operating premises meeting Vehicle Code 250's chop-shop definition. The activity concerns vehicles or parts known to be illegally obtained by theft, fraud or conspiracy to defraud, for the specified identity-concealment or sale/disposal purpose. An ordinary repair or dismantling business is not a chop shop merely because it handles parts.
penalty: Misdemeanor or felony. Felony punishment: 2, 3 or 4 years under Penal Code 1170(h), a fine up to $50,000, or both. Misdemeanor punishment: up to 364 days in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. Section 1170(h) custody is ordinarily in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. The felony fine ceiling does not become the misdemeanor fine ceiling. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: Knowing and intentional ownership or operation, with the illegal-origin knowledge and purpose required by the statutory chop-shop definition.

title: Altering vehicle identification numbers for sale or transfer
summary: Knowingly altering, counterfeiting, defacing, destroying, disguising, falsifying, forging, obliterating or removing a vehicle identification number, intending to misrepresent identity or prevent identification, for sale, transfer, import or export. A single vehicle or part can satisfy this statute; it does not import 10803's more-than-one-vehicle threshold.
penalty: Misdemeanor or felony. Felony punishment: 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under Penal Code 1170(h), a fine up to $25,000, or both. Misdemeanor punishment: up to 364 days in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. Section 1170(h) custody is ordinarily in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. The felony fine ceiling does not become the misdemeanor fine ceiling. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: Knowing alteration, specific identity-concealment intent, and the specified sale/transfer/import/export purpose.

title: Dealing in multiple vehicles or parts with altered identifiers
summary: Buying with intent to resell, disposing of, selling or transferring more than one motor vehicle, or parts from more than one motor vehicle, knowing the identification numbers were altered or removed for identity concealment. Several parts from only one vehicle do not establish the more-than-one-vehicle requirement. Section 10804 excludes specified good-faith scrap processing and qualifying owner/authorized-possessor situations involving recovery or law-enforcement knowledge; these exceptions must be checked.
penalty: Misdemeanor or felony. Felony punishment: 2, 4 or 6 years under Penal Code 1170(h), a fine up to $60,000, or both. Misdemeanor punishment: up to 364 days in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. Section 1170(h) custody is ordinarily in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. The felony fine ceiling does not become the misdemeanor fine ceiling. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: Knowledge of altered identifiers and their identity-concealment purpose; buying additionally requires intent to resell.

title: Possessing multiple vehicles or parts with altered identifiers for distribution
summary: Possessing more than one motor vehicle, or parts from more than one motor vehicle, for sale, transfer, import or export, knowing the identification numbers were altered or removed for identity concealment. Several parts from only one vehicle do not establish the more-than-one-vehicle requirement. Section 10804 excludes specified good-faith scrap processing and qualifying owner/authorized-possessor situations involving recovery or law-enforcement knowledge; these exceptions must be checked.
penalty: Misdemeanor or felony. Felony punishment: 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under Penal Code 1170(h), a fine up to $30,000, or both. Misdemeanor punishment: up to 364 days in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. Section 1170(h) custody is ordinarily in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. The felony fine ceiling does not become the misdemeanor fine ceiling. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: Knowing possession with the specified distribution purpose and knowledge of the identity-concealing alteration.

title: Unauthorized alteration or stamping of vehicle identification marks
summary: Intentionally defacing, destroying or altering a vehicle number or identification mark used for registration without written DMV authorization, or placing or stamping a number or mark other than one assigned by DMV. Section 10750(b) preserves DMV-authorized restoration of the original VIN and ordinary manufacturer marking of new vehicles or parts. This is distinct from the sale-related concealment offense in 10802.
penalty: Misdemeanor under Vehicle Code 40000.9, with the default in 42002: up to 6 months in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: Intentional alteration or the prohibited placement/stamping; the authorization and manufacturer exceptions must be assessed.

title: Dealing in or possessing a vehicle or part with a removed identifier
summary: Knowingly buying, selling, offering for sale, receiving or possessing a vehicle or component with a manufacturer identification number removed, defaced, altered or destroyed. The statute excepts a DMV-assigned or approved replacement identification number and qualifying scrap-metal processors under (f). The property-disposition hearing described in (b)-(e) is a separate civil proceeding, not itself this criminal charge.
penalty: Misdemeanor under Vehicle Code 40000.9, with the default in 42002: up to 6 months in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: Knowing conduct involving the altered or removed manufacturer identification number; possession alone does not eliminate the knowledge requirement.

title: Failure to report property damage caused by a runaway parked vehicle
summary: A person who parked a vehicle must meet 20002's notification and reporting duties if, before it is driven again, it becomes a runaway vehicle and causes property damage. Merely owning the vehicle is not this parking-based branch. This entry does not cover a nondriving passenger's control-based liability.
penalty: Misdemeanor under 20002(c): up to 6 months in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. This is the property-damage reporting branch; injury/death hit-and-run punishment must not be imported. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: Failure to comply with the statutory notification/reporting duties after the specified runaway-vehicle accident; knowledge and ability to comply must be assessed from the facts.

title: Vehicle tampering or damage without owner consent
summary: Willfully injuring or tampering with a vehicle or its contents, or breaking or removing a vehicle part, without the owner's consent. This entry does not require assuming an intent to permanently steal the entire vehicle.
penalty: Misdemeanor under Vehicle Code 40000.9, with the default in 42002: up to 6 months in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: Willful prohibited interference or damage without owner consent.

title: Unauthorized use or removal of parts by a vehicle custodian
summary: A person entrusted with storage, care, safekeeping, custody or possession of a vehicle subject to registration takes, hires, runs, drives or uses it, or removes a part, without the owner's consent. The custodial relationship distinguishes this provision from generic vehicle theft.
penalty: Misdemeanor: up to 364 days in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. Penal Code 18.5 limits the statute's stated one-year misdemeanor term to 364 days. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: Unauthorized use or part removal by a person with the statutory custody/possession relationship; owner consent must be assessed.

title: False or fraudulent vehicle-theft report
summary: Making or filing a false or fraudulent theft report for a vehicle required to be registered, with a law-enforcement agency and with intent to deceive. A mistaken report without that intent is not enough.
penalty: Ordinary misdemeanor under Vehicle Code 40000.9/42002: up to 6 months in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both. A prior conviction of this same subdivision activates 10501(b): 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under Penal Code 1170(h), or up to 364 days in county jail. The special repeat provision does not state a fine. Where no other fine is prescribed, Penal Code 672 permits an additional fine up to $1,000 for a misdemeanor or $10,000 for a felony; confirm its application to the charged branch. Section 1170(h) custody is ordinarily in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. A generic prior conviction does not establish this repeat branch. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, assessments, restitution and case-specific sentencing rules require separate review.
mentalState: Intent to deceive in making or filing the false/fraudulent theft report.
